verdict: Avoid new steel re-rolling and TMT exposure in Salem for now; lend only to branded, integrated re-rollers with verified power and scrap linkages, and only on tight monthly structure.
title: Salem steel re-rolling & TMT: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Salem re-roller buys sponge iron, scrap and billets, melts or reheats, rolls TMT bars, and sells to dealers and builders. **Cash is made in the spread between scrap/billet cost and TMT realisation, not in volume.** Power and fuel are the swing cost; the rolling mill is the capex. Working capital sits in inventory (billets, finished bars) and dealer credit. **So when a proposal lands, check the conversion spread and power tariff first; if the unit cannot show a spread over billet cost, ask for the last six months of invoice-level realisation.**

## What has changed now
Tamil Nadu GST collections fell 3.2% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, a 9.3 pp gap [D] — a local demand and compliance stress signal. Brent at $113/bbl sits above the $75–100 band [D], which raises freight and power-linked costs for a gas/oil-linked re-roller. **The data call is AVOID at 37 [D], and the local news flow does not offset it.** Salem's own coverage is thin: local reports are about government contractors chasing highway arrears [1], and the SAIL Salem and Salem Steel topic pages carry no usable operating data [2][3]. **Treat Salem-specific evidence as absent and lean on first principles plus peers.**

## Where the growth is
Peer results are strong and recent: Steel Exchange India clocked ~₹340 crore revenue in Q2 FY27, up ~45% YoY [6]; Rathi Steel reported over ₹200 crore, up over 30% YoY with volume up ~28.86% [7]; JSW Steel's Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 20% with gearing at 0.42 [5]. **Pursue branded TMT re-rollers with own billet linkage and dealer pull, not job-work rollers.** The ICRA note on Captain Steel shows brand ambassadors and national advertising command a premium over market rate [9] — that pricing power is the borrower type to back. **Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, monthly power bills, and quarterly GST returns; if power consumption per tonne rises without a volume reason, ask for the furnace log.** Rating reports flag sudden price fluctuations hitting margins [10] and moderately high working capital needs [11]; the MITC and Kubair notes show leverage can move fast (gearing 1.80x from 1.40x) [10][8]. **So cap total debt at a level the conversion spread can service in a bad quarter, and take a personal guarantee plus hypothecation of stock.**

## Early-warning signs
- Monthly GST returns (monthly): two consecutive months of falling turnover with flat power draw -> stop fresh disbursement and inspect stock. - Power bill per tonne (monthly): a jump without a tariff revision -> ask for the revised cost sheet and re-price the limit. - Dealer receivable ageing (monthly): beyond the agreed credit period -> shift to cash-and-carry sales. - Billet purchase invoices (monthly): a shift to costlier spot buys -> check the spread and cut exposure.
